batch11.title: Batch FAISS face queries and resolve shared gallery identities together
batch11.body:
## Tickets
Self-contained search performance improvement.

## What has been done
A multi-face ANN search currently calls FAISS once per face and repeats gallery-name lookups for identities shared by those faces. This serializes independent HNSW queries and adds database round trips.

Submit the face embeddings as one FAISS query matrix, then resolve the unique matched identities together through the database adapter's existing lookup method. Preserve per-face result order, empty matches, thresholds, missing-neighbor filtering, requested limits, and facial-area metadata.

## How to test
Added real FAISS/SQLite integration coverage for normalized and unnormalized embeddings, verification and similarity searches, single and multiple faces, default and explicit limits, missing neighbors, empty batches, and shared identities. The numerical and returned-record results are compared with individual face searches.

[Validation run](https://github.com/Afloat16/deepface/actions/runs/43858024543) on Python 3.10 and 3.12:
- Original production source: 13 regression failures and 15 passing controls.
- Updated source, including the adjacent FAISS missing-neighbor, face-order, and SQLite suites: 48 passed in each environment.
- Repository-pinned Pylint: 10.00/10; MyPy: 145 source files passed; test formatting passed.

The same run measures a real FAISS 1.16.0 HNSW index with 10,000 128-dimensional vectors, 128 query faces, k=20, and two FAISS threads. Across seven repeated complete datastore searches, median time changed from 36.42 to 22.23 ms on Python 3.10 and from 29.94 to 17.87 ms on Python 3.12. These measurements use precomputed synthetic embeddings and an actual SQLite gallery; they exclude face detection and neural inference. No timing threshold is asserted in the regression tests.

batch12.title: Batch detected face embeddings during verification
batch12.body:
## Tickets
Self-contained verification performance improvement.

## What has been done
Verification currently calls representation separately for every detected face, even though representation already supports batched inference. A group photo therefore launches the recognition model repeatedly with singleton inputs.

Pass the already-extracted face crops to representation together, once per input image. Keep the original face order, BGR conversion, normalization, facial-area metadata, scalar custom-distance callbacks, and empty-face behavior. Check every anti-spoofing verdict before running that image's recognition batch.

## How to test
[Validation run](https://github.com/Afloat16/deepface/actions/runs/43859782785), Python 3.10 and 3.12:
- Original production source: 11 regression failures and 14 passing controls.
- Patched source plus the existing threshold, angular-distance, and empty-representation suites: 93 passed in each environment.
- Pylint 2.15.10: 10.00/10; MyPy 1.14.1: 145 source files passed; new-test formatting passed.

The new tests cover single and multiple faces, all four built-in metrics and a scalar custom metric, two normalization modes, best-match facial areas, empty extraction, precomputed embeddings, and a spoof later in the detected face list.

A separate case loads the real pretrained FaceNet ONNX weights and compares eight-face results with individual representations. With two CPU inference threads and five measured repetitions, recognition/preprocessing median time changed from 103.12 to 79.35 ms on Python 3.10 / ONNX Runtime 1.23.2 and from 72.90 to 63.26 ms on Python 3.12 / ONNX Runtime 1.32.0. Model forward calls changed from eight singleton calls to one batch. The observed embeddings were identical in these runs.

The benchmark uses deterministic synthetic face crops; detection is replaced at the extraction boundary. It measures the recognition/preprocessing stage, not detection time or model accuracy, and asserts no timing threshold.

batch13.title: Close Pinecone request clients after database operations
batch13.body:
## Tickets
Self-contained Pinecone resource-lifetime fix.

## What has been done
Each database operation creates a fresh Pinecone index client. These clients are never closed, and the adapter's own `close()` is a no-op. With the current SDK this leaves the independent HTTP connection pools alive after requests finish.

Close the operation-local index clients after insert, search, single-record read, and gallery read, including error and early-return paths. Close the control-plane client when the adapter is closed, while allowing older SDK versions that have no control-plane close method. Public searches continue to leave caller-supplied control-plane clients open.

## How to test
[Validation run](https://github.com/Afloat16/deepface/actions/runs/43866791770):
- Python 3.12 / Pinecone 10.1.0: original source has 12 failures and 2 passing controls.
- Python 3.10 / Pinecone 8.0.0: original source has 11 failures and 3 passing controls.
- Patched source plus existing index-name and registration-ownership tests: 32 passed in each environment.
- Repository-pinned Pylint: 10.00/10; MyPy: 145 source files passed; Black formatting passed.

The tests use actual SDK clients and HTTP/1.1 connections against a loopback service. They cover successful calls, service errors, empty/missing results, ownership, and repeated searches. In Pinecone 10.1.0, twenty searches change from zero to twenty native index-close calls and from 21 live HTTP connections to one remaining caller-owned control-plane connection.

Pinecone 8's native `Index.close()` closes its worker pool but does not clear its HTTP pool. The legacy checks verify native-close calls and unchanged results; this patch does not claim to fix that SDK-internal socket limitation. The service and recognition boundary are fixtures.

batch14.title: Keep high-dimensional embeddings usable in pgvector
batch14.body:
## Tickets
Self-contained pgvector registration fix.

## What has been done
The default VGG-Face model produces 4,096-dimensional embeddings, but pgvector's HNSW index for the `vector` type supports at most 2,000 dimensions. Initialization currently tries to create that index unconditionally, so registration and even an empty-gallery search fail with `column cannot have more than 2000 dimensions for hnsw index`.

Create the table with its full embedding dimensions and skip only the unsupported HNSW index above that limit. Log that these galleries use an exact scan. Models at or below 2,000 dimensions keep their existing HNSW indexes and distance operators. The vectors are not truncated or quantized.

The limit is documented in [pgvector's HNSW support](https://github.com/pgvector/pgvector#hnsw).

## How to test
[Validation run](https://github.com/Afloat16/deepface/actions/runs/43862495314), Python 3.10 and 3.12, real PostgreSQL 16.16 and pgvector extension 0.8.7:
- Original production source: 8 failing regression cases and 5 passing controls.
- Patched source plus existing datastore and connection-ownership regressions: 52 passed in each environment.
- Pylint 2.15.10: 10.00/10; MyPy 1.14.1: 145 source files passed; test formatting passed.

The integration tests exercise 128, 2,000, 2,001, and 4,096 dimensions with both distance operators; inspect actual index definitions; check stored vector dimensions and values through SQL; compare returned nearest neighbors and distances; and cover the public registration path, empty galleries, and invalid column dimensions.

Recognition is replaced at the embedding/metadata boundary. PostgreSQL schema creation, storage, index creation, and searches use the actual driver and database. The high-dimensional fallback is exact scanning and can be slower than indexed search on a large gallery.

batch15.title: Read gallery IDs from current Pinecone SDK listing pages
batch15.body:
## Tickets
Self-contained Pinecone SDK compatibility fix.

## What has been done
The current Pinecone SDK yields `ListResponse` pages from `Index.list()`; each page contains vector records whose IDs are in `item.id`. The existing code extends the ID list with those records and passes them to `fetch`, which rejects them. Full-gallery reads and exact searches therefore fail with the current SDK.

Extract IDs from native listing pages and retain support for older SDKs that yield lists of ID strings. Pagination and fetch batch sizes are unchanged.

## How to test
[Validation run](https://github.com/Afloat16/deepface/actions/runs/43866246592):
- Python 3.12 / Pinecone 10.1.0: original source has 6 failures and 2 passing controls; patched source plus adjacent tests has 26 passes.
- Python 3.10 / Pinecone 8.0.0: all 8 new tests already pass on the original source, and all 26 selected tests pass after the change.
- Repository-pinned Pylint: 10.00/10; MyPy: 145 source files passed; Black formatting passed.

Tests use actual SDK clients against a loopback HTTP service. They cover multiple listing pages, independent fetch batch sizes, exact record IDs and metadata, empty galleries, propagated service errors, and the public exact-search path. The service and recognition boundary are fixtures; SDK serialization, response decoding, pagination, and distance calculations are real.

batch16.title: Decode embeddings returned by pgvector Python 0.5
batch16.body:
## Tickets
Self-contained pgvector driver compatibility fix.

## What has been done
pgvector Python 0.5 changed Psycopg's decoded `vector` value from a NumPy array to a `Vector` object. That object is not iterable, so the existing `list(value)` calls raise `TypeError: 'Vector' object is not iterable`. This breaks single-identity reads, full-gallery reads, exact searches, and identification with the current driver.

Use the driver's `to_list()` method when available and retain the existing conversion for older array-returning drivers. The production change is two return-value conversions.

The driver change is recorded in [pgvector Python's 0.5.0 changelog](https://github.com/pgvector/pgvector-python/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md).

## How to test
[Validation run](https://github.com/Afloat16/deepface/actions/runs/43862864470), using real PostgreSQL 16.16, pgvector extension 0.8.7, and Psycopg 3.3.9:
- Python 3.12 / pgvector Python 0.5.1: original source has 8 failures and 3 passing controls; patched source plus adjacent regressions has 50 passes.
- Python 3.10 / pgvector Python 0.4.2: all 11 new cases already pass on the original source, and all 50 selected cases pass after the change.
- Repository-pinned Pylint: 10.00/10; MyPy: 145 source files passed; test formatting passed.

The tests read actual database values through both decoder generations, verify single-row and streamed batch results, exercise public exact search and identification, and preserve missing-identity, empty-gallery, and native ANN-search behavior. Recognition is replaced at the embedding boundary; database reads, decoded values, and distance calculations are real.

batch17.title: Preserve mixed-case image paths during registration
batch17.body:
## Tickets
Self-contained registration identity fix.

## What has been done
Registering a valid image such as `Photo.JPG` currently assigns a random UUID as its name, while `Photo.jpg` retains its path. The image loader and gallery discovery already accept these extensions without regard to case, so later searches lose the source path solely because of extension casing.

Compare the extension in lowercase while storing the original path unchanged. Explicit image names and UUID identifiers for arrays, file objects, and base64 data keep their existing behavior.

## How to test
[Validation run](https://github.com/Afloat16/deepface/actions/runs/43866203772), Python 3.10 and 3.12:
- Original source: 7 failures and 8 passing controls in each environment.
- Patched source plus existing registration connection tests: 29 passed in each environment.
- Pylint 2.15.10: 10.00/10; MyPy 1.14.1: 145 source files passed; Black formatting passed.

The regressions write real JPEG/PNG files, use OpenCV decoding and normal preprocessing, register them in SQLite, and check stored names and public search results. They cover upper/mixed/lowercase extensions, mixed batches, explicit names, and non-path input types. Only the recognition model is replaced with a small deterministic fixture; image loading, database operations, and distance calculations are real.

batch18.title: Serialize concurrent requests to shared MediaPipe graphs
batch18.body:
### What has been done

Cached MediaPipe detectors share a native Solutions graph. `process` updates the graph timestamp and output dictionary, so concurrent requests can submit duplicate timestamps, leave the graph unusable, or receive another image's detections.

Guard each detector's `process` call with an instance lock. Separate detector instances can still infer in parallel, and a failed request releases the lock. Update the color-order fixture to use normal client initialization.

### How to test

[Validation run](https://github.com/Afloat16/deepface/actions/runs/43869361080) on Python 3.10 and 3.12 with MediaPipe 0.10.21:

- The base version has **3 failures and 4 passing controls**: a crossed-result regression and duplicate timestamps in the real short-range and full-range native graphs.
- The fix has **9 passing tests** per Python version, including native inference, separate-instance concurrency, exception recovery, existing color-order coverage, and SSD controls.
- Pylint **10.00/10**, MyPy clean across **145 source files**, and Black checks pass.

The native tests retain the actual graph and packet builder; they pause one request at packet creation to reproduce the overlapping timestamp updates deterministically.

batch19.title: Keep MediaPipe installations compatible with the Solutions detector
batch19.body:
## Tickets

No linked issue.

### What has been done

The optional MediaPipe requirement and installation hint allow current releases that no longer expose `mp.solutions`. Both the 0.10.30 and 1.2.3 wheels fail immediately when DeepFace builds the detector, before any inference can run.

Constrain the optional requirement to `mediapipe>=0.8.7.3,<0.10.30`, and use that same command when the dependency is absent or its legacy Solutions API is unavailable. The existing short-range and full-range detector modes remain supported.

## How to test

[Python 3.10 and 3.12 validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/deepface/actions/runs/43872136361):

- The original implementation has 2 failing regression tests with 4 passing controls. Both actual incompatible SDK wheels reproduce `AttributeError`; the change reports the compatible installation command.
- The declared requirement resolves to and installs 0.10.21. Both native detector modes find the face in the repository's `img1.jpg` and return no faces for a blank image.
- 7 unit tests pass on each Python version, including the existing color-order and SSD version checks. Black passes; the upstream Pylint and MyPy commands pass on Python 3.10 (145 source files).

batch20.title: Keep gallery caches separate for different detection policies
batch20.body:
## Tickets

N/A

### What has been done

Gallery embeddings depend on `enforce_detection`, but the cache filename does not include that policy. A cache built with `False` retains whole-image fallback embeddings when a later call requests `True`. In the reverse order, switching to `False` keeps missing-embedding rows at infinite distance instead of computing the permitted fallback.

Include the detection policy in non-`skip` cache names. Default and explicit `True` use the same cache, while `detector_backend="skip"` continues to share its existing cache across both values. Missing-detection rows and their infinite-distance behavior remain intact. Update the existing refresh-disabled regression's cache filename.

**Cache compatibility:** existing non-`skip` caches need a one-time rebuild with `refresh_database=True` for each policy used. Existing files are left untouched. `refresh_database=False` requires the corresponding new policy cache to exist; it cannot safely reuse a legacy cache whose detection policy is unknown.

### How to test

- `python -m pytest -q tests/unit/test_gallery_detection_policy.py tests/unit/test_find_color_consistency.py tests/unit/test_cached_gallery_query.py`
- [Validation on Python 3.10 and 3.12](https://github.com/Afloat16/deepface/actions/runs/43876255050): 6 regressions fail and 2 controls pass on the base revision; 18 checks pass after the fix, including real OpenCV detection, native SFace ONNX embeddings, and the existing refresh-disabled cache test using SFace in place of VGG weights.
- The native reproduction switches a blank gallery image between distance `11.175977` with fallback enabled and `inf` with enforcement enabled, in both call orders. Matching cached reads work without listing the gallery.
- Pylint: 10.00/10; mypy: 145 source files pass; new validation tests pass Black with line length 100.
